## RED evidence (F-013)

**New suite:** `apps/cli/src/commands/cli.dashOptionValues.test.ts` (16 tests, process-level, spawns the shared `dist/cli.js` built once by the T36 globalSetup).

### Failing now (intended behaviour, 10)

| # | Test | Expected | Actual today |
|---|------|----------|--------------|
| 1 | accepts a `--profile` value that begins with '-' | exit 0 / `ok` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 2 | accepts a `--relay-url` value that begins with '-' ... | exit 2 / `INVALID_CONFIGURATION` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 3 | accepts a `--store-key-env` value that begins with '-' ... | exit 2 / `INVALID_CONFIGURATION` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 4 | accepts an `--out` value that begins with '-' | exit 0 / `ok` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 5 | accepts a `--from` value that begins with '-' | exit 0 / `ok` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 6 | accepts a `--to` value that begins with '-' and carries it verbatim into the trust layer | exit 3 / `CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED`, identical to the same run without the leading '-' | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 7 | accepts a `--text` value that begins with '-' | exit 3 / `CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED` (trust, not parsing, is what stops it) | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 8 | accepts a `--message-id` value that begins with '-' ... | exit 2 / `INVALID_MESSAGE_ID` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 9 | accepts a `--with` value that begins with '-' | exit 0 / `ok`, `data.entries == []` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |
| 10 | delivers dash-leading bodies, including one spelled exactly like a known flag | both sends exit 0, both bodies readable verbatim through `history` | exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS` |

Exact headline failing assertion (test 6, the F-013 blocker):

```
expect(outcome(dashed)).toMatchObject({ code: 3, errorCode: "CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED" });
// AssertionError: expected { code: 2, errorCode: 'INVALID_ARGUMENTS', timedOut: false }
//                 to match object { code: 3, errorCode: 'CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED' }
```

### Passing now (fail-closed guards + separator pins, 6)

- still rejects an unknown flag, with or without a dash-leading value -> exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`
- still rejects an option whose value is missing at the end of the argument list (`--text`, `--with`, `--profile` trailing) -> exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`
- still rejects a repeated option, including when the repeat carries a dash-leading value -> exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`
- still rejects an option the command does not accept, an unknown command, and a stray positional -> exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`
- treats a bare trailing `--` as a no-op -> exit 0 / `ok`
- fails closed on any operand after `--` (no command takes positional operands) -> exit 2 / `INVALID_ARGUMENTS`

These six are what stop the fix from being obtained by simply turning `strict: true` off: Node's `parseArgs` raises the SAME `ERR_PARSE_ARGS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE` for a dash-leading value and for an option whose value is missing at the end of argv, so the fix has to separate those two cases rather than suppress the error class.

### Determinism

Every dash-leading value is a fixed literal in the `dash` constant table (e.g. `--to "-DashRecipientIdentity000000000000000000000A"`). Nothing waits for a randomly generated base64url identity to start with '-', which is what made `pnpm test` look intermittently red.

### Contract preservation

The local `outcome()` helper asserts, on every single run in the suite, that stdout holds exactly one line parsing to one JSON object with the documented `ok`/`error.code` shape; `redacted()` asserts by boolean that no store key, private-key field name, `ciphertext` or message body ever appears in stdout+stderr. No plaintext body, ciphertext, store key or HTTP request body is printed anywhere in the suite or in this report.

### Routing audit

`graph_used: no (not-relevant - target files were named in the dispatch)`, `wiki_used: no (not-relevant - defect and contract fully specified by the dispatch and docs/requirements/echolet-cli-prototype/specification.md)`, `ctx_used: yes (keryx ctx read / keryx ctx rg / keryx ctx run)`, `raw_rg_used: no`.

acceptance.criterion: F-013 (blocker): a deterministic test proves that `send --to <identity>` succeeds when the identity_id begins with '-'. The test must currently FAIL.
acceptance.evidence: Two tests pin it and both fail today with exit 2 / INVALID_ARGUMENTS: 'accepts a --to value that begins with '-' and carries it verbatim into the trust layer' (expects exit 3 / CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED, and expects the outcome to be byte-identical to the same send with the leading '-' stripped) and 'delivers dash-leading bodies, including one spelled exactly like a known flag' (a full trusted send through a relay stub, expecting exit 0). Deliberate deviation: a fully successful `send --to` against a REAL identity whose base64url encoding begins with '-' cannot be built deterministically, because identity_id is derived from a generated public key and cannot be chosen. Forcing it would mean regenerating identities until one starts with '-' - exactly the 1-in-64 sampling the dispatch forbids. Instead the dash-leading recipient is proven to reach the trust layer verbatim (CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED, identical to the non-dash control), and end-to-end success for the same command shape is proven separately by the trusted send test. Flagged for reviewer judgement.

acceptance.criterion: The test class is enumerated, not sampled: every string-valued option is covered with a fixed literal value beginning with '-'.
acceptance.evidence: All 9 string-valued options in cliOptions (cli.ts:24-36) have their own named test: --profile, --relay-url, --store-key-env, --out, --from, --to, --text, --message-id, --with. --json and --yes are boolean and take no value. Values come from the fixed `dash` literal table; nothing is randomly generated. The documented surface in docs/requirements/echolet-cli-prototype/specification.md adds no further string option.

acceptance.criterion: A `--text` value beginning with '-' is accepted as message content, including a value that looks like a known flag, and is not reinterpreted as an option.
acceptance.evidence: 'delivers dash-leading bodies, including one spelled exactly like a known flag' sends both `--text "-SYNTHETIC_DASH_TEXT"` and `--text "--profile"` over a relay stub to a trusted contact, expects exit 0 for both, then reads them back through `history` and asserts (by boolean containment, never by printing) that both bodies survive verbatim. The `--profile` case is argv-adjacent to a real later `--profile <dir>`, so a fix that swallows the flag instead of the value fails this test.

acceptance.criterion: Genuinely invalid input still fails closed with exit 2: unknown flag, missing required value, repeated option keep INVALID_ARGUMENTS.
acceptance.evidence: Four guard tests, all passing today and required to stay passing: unknown flag (bare and with a dash-leading value), missing value at end of argv for --text/--with/--profile, repeated option (including a repeat whose second value is dash-leading), and option-not-allowed-for-command / unknown command / stray positional. Node's parseArgs raises the same ERR_PARSE_ARGS_INVALID_OPTION_VALUE for a dash value and for a trailing option with no value, so disabling strict parsing cannot satisfy both the RED tests and these guards.

acceptance.criterion: `--` end-of-options handling, if the fix introduces it, is pinned by a test rather than left implicit.
acceptance.evidence: Two tests in describe('end-of-options separator (F-013)'): a bare trailing `--` is a no-op (exit 0 / ok), and any operand after `--` fails closed with exit 2 / INVALID_ARGUMENTS because no command on the surface takes positional operands (covers `-- extra`, `-- --json`, and `-- --to other`). Both pass today, so the fix cannot silently start ignoring post-separator operands.

acceptance.criterion: The existing exit-code contract is unchanged for every other case, and one JSON object on stdout / redacted diagnostics on stderr still holds.
acceptance.evidence: The suite's outcome() helper asserts on every run that stdout is exactly one line parsing to a single non-array JSON object with ok true or an /^[A-Z_]+$/ error.code, and that the child did not time out. redacted() asserts by boolean that the store key, identitySecretKey/deviceSecretKey/sessionSecretKey/"seed"/ciphertext and the message body never appear in stdout+stderr.

acceptance.criterion: All currently-passing tests stay green; no existing assertion is weakened or deleted.
acceptance.evidence: `npx vitest run` in apps/cli: 13 test files, 69 tests, 10 failed / 59 passed. The only failing file is the new cli.dashOptionValues.test.ts. cli.test.ts, cli.processFailures.test.ts, test/e2e/two-process.test.ts and all runtime/transport suites pass. No existing file was edited; vitest.config.ts and test/globalSetup.ts were read only. `pnpm typecheck` in apps/cli exits 0.

Bounded RED run of the new suite alone: 16 tests, 10 failed / 6 passed.

questions.question: Is a dash-leading `--to` value that reaches the trust layer (exit 3 CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED, identical to the non-dash control) accepted as proof for the F-013 headline criterion, given that a real identity_id beginning with '-' cannot be chosen deterministically?
questions.why: identity_id is encodeBase64Url(publicKey) and cannot be steered; the only way to obtain a genuine dash-leading identity is to regenerate identities until one appears, which reintroduces exactly the 1-in-64 sampling the dispatch forbids. The suite therefore proves (a) the dash-leading recipient reaches the trust layer verbatim and (b) an end-to-end trusted send with dash-leading content succeeds.
